title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis
population: 15 studies with 34 treatment groups; participant characteristics are not detailed in the abstract.
key_findings: Treated as a continuous variable, more weekly sets were associated with larger gains in muscle size: each extra set added about 0.023 to the effect size, roughly 0.37 percentage points of growth.
Comparing the higher-volume and lower-volume arms within each study, higher volume gave an effect size about 0.24 larger, roughly 3.9 percentage points more growth.
Grouped as fewer than 5, 5 to 9, and 10 or more weekly sets per muscle, the difference was only a trend (p = 0.074).
The authors read the pattern as a graded dose-response: more volume, more hypertrophy, within the range the studies covered.
methods: Systematic review with meta-regression of weekly sets per muscle against measures of muscle mass.
limitations: Only 15 studies; the three-category analysis did not reach significance; the abstract does not report the training status, sex or age of participants, and the relationship can only be read within the volumes the studies tested.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
